methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
AMP Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Matanya Horowitz that has raised $439.1M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of nine private robotics firms and one public company (277810.KQ), including peers at Series B stage (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B) and Seed stage (Walden Robotics at $1.1B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. The Stage-Progression method uses a $30M base proxy derived from total raised, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $60M. The Peer-Median method references the median valuation of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers at $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B. The disparity between methods reflects AMP's position relative to more mature Series B comparables and earlier-stage peers.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $51M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median estimate of $880M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty regarding stage-adjusted positioning: Stage-Progression suggests significantly lower valuation anchored to capital raised, while Peer-Median suggests meaningfully higher valuation aligned with later-stage competitors. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory relative to comparable firms, fundraising dynamics at Series B entry, and whether AMP's capital efficiency and growth profile warrant premium or discount to peer medians.
